cleanup.interpretation: The harness only claimed tracked Popen cleanup. Actions later killed an orphan nvda process. Do not turn that claim into complete descendant cleanup or a successful shutdown.

diagnosis.primary_classification: Harness observation/routing defect, not evidence that the product menu is absent
diagnosis.cause: The supplement bound EVT_MENU_HIGHLIGHT_ALL only to tray.menu and tray.toolsMenu. NVDA SysTrayIcon invokes its own PopupMenu. On wxMSW that method pushes the TaskBarIcon onto the hidden popup-owner window's event chain. The observer therefore omitted the actual popup owner; the run recorded zero highlight events even as NVDA announced the expected label.

primary_sources.observation: Exact wxWidgets version from the actual NVDA log: wxTaskBarIcon::PopupMenu calls m_win->PushEventHandler(this), then m_win->PopupMenu(menu), then pops that handler.
Native menu events route through menu-associated/owning event handlers; GetMenuId returns the menu-specific identifier.

diagnosis.secondary_controller_defect: The outer controller waited for process exit and raised on nonzero returncode before assigning phases.resume. That concealed the already written primary menu-timeout receipt from the aggregate report.
diagnosis.fatal_exit_classification: Real fatal NVDA process result, not a benign or accepted shutdown code. The available log was overwritten by a subsequent startup; no preserved crash stack/dump proves the exact origin of the callback exception. It must remain an unresolved separate failure until a real rerun demonstrates normal exit and cleanup.

ownership_hardening_after_diagnosis.implementation: Local narrow OwnedNvdaJob with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE and no breakaway. Each exact nvda.exe Popen starts CREATE_SUSPENDED, is assigned using its already-held process handle, then resumes using that same handle. Descendants inherit the job before they can be spawned; no PID rediscovery or broad process kill.
ownership_hardening_after_diagnosis.cleanup: Held job accounting must reach zero active processes before endpoint removal. A bounded grace allows ordinary worker teardown; TerminateJobObject is the final cleanup path and remains an explicit failed normal-shutdown gate, even after zero active is verified. Error paths close the held job; failed assignment also reaps the exact still-suspended child handle.
